## role-task-labels: roles_overview names a role's tasks as "<role> #N"

- `local` (Ops #712; follow-up to the message audit, gap R6d, the owner picked "Both"; plan approved in Ops lead, 2026-10-31). Hypothesis H-R6d (`~/kept-from-tmp/2026-10-31/message-audit-gaps/GAPS.md`, R6d): text that leaves a department carried a bare "#N" although 348 of 666 task numbers repeat across departments, so receipts and reminders were ambiguous. Naming a role's tasks "<role> #N" (the name the host already resolves refs by) in `queue_add`'s result, the rule 24 reminder (both pi-queue) and `roles_overview` (here) should make receipts carry the role: tests assert `<role> #\d+`; live, for 7 days, receipts without a role ("Queued as #N" in `role-messages.json`) fall below 10%; wrong if they stay above 25% (then R5's native receipt is the fix).
- `server/task-queue.ts` `roleTaskRefLabel(ref, role)`: `taskRefLabel`'s variant (paired with pi-queue `queue-fields.ts` `roleRefLabel`): a task of the queue reads "<role> #N", another queue's task and every task of a queue without a role read as `taskRefLabel` says. `server/roles-overview-tool.ts`: the task lines (at work, waiting, dropped), "question in task <role> #N" and a TL;DR line's "task <role> #N" use it with the section's role id. No other wording changes; refs are parsed and routed as before; the Roles page and the Queue panel are unchanged.
- Checks: `tests/unit/roles-overview-tool.test.ts`: the exact-line cases now expect "temper #7" and "frontend #1", and "names every task as <role> #N" checks both views for no bare "#N"; 5 of 14 fail on the old code, all pass on the new.
- Undo: revert this commit and `pi-web-deploy` it (and revert pi-queue's companion commit + `pi-web-deploy restart`).
